extracted.intended_audience: IP litigators, in-house counsel, law firms, patent litigators, and legal-analytics users
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing U.S. patent litigation trends and metrics (district courts, PTAB, federal appeals) using Lex Machina data, with emphasis on comparisons over the 2021–2023 period and descriptive breakdowns (districts, judges, parties, timing, outcomes, damages, PTAB flow).

rubrics_metrics.name: What is a Patent Case?
rubrics_metrics.description: A case with one or more claims involving patent infringement, invalidity, or unenforceability brought under 35 USC § 271. False marking, inventorship, or contract cases are not included in the patent case type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition determines which dockets are included in the dataset and analysis; exclude false-marking, inventorship, and contract matters from the 'patent case' category.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-Volume Plaintiff —
rubrics_metrics.description: High-Volume Plaintiffs (HVPs) are plaintiffs that file at least 10 patent cases (excluding ANDA cases) within a 365-day period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a party is determined to be a high-volume filer, this tag applies to all of the party's patent cases (excluding ANDA cases) in which the party is a plaintiff (or defendant in a declaratory judgment case), regardless of when the cases were filed. Lex Machina treats HVP as a behavior-based classification to avoid subjective NPE/PAE labels; analyses should consider results both including and excluding HVPs (the report shows that excluding HVPs yields steadier filing trends).

rubrics_metrics.name: ANDA —
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent cases prompted by the filing of an ANDA or paper NDA that includes a Paragraph IV Certification (incentivized by the Hatch-Waxman Act's first to file exclusivity provisions for prospective generic drug makers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ANDA cases, submitting an application to the FDA to market a generic drug constitutes an act of infringement. ANDA cases have distinct filing and timing characteristics (e.g., shorter time-to-trial but longer time-to-termination) and should be analyzed separately from general patent cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Case Tags / Filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: Lex Machina uses machine learning and natural language processing to create case tags that identify certain claims in a case and enable filtering (e.g., general patent cases, patent cases excluding high-volume plaintiffs, ANDA cases, PTAB cases, patent appellate cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply tags to enable apples-to-apples comparisons. Users can further apply custom tags in their research; filters materially affect trends (e.g., HVP exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases Filed (yearly filing counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of patent cases filed in U.S. District Courts (2014–2023) and Federal Appellate dockets originating from patent cases; the report focuses on comparisons across the three-year period from the beginning of 2021 to the end of 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret filing trends with awareness of drivers (e.g., HVP activity, venue rules, industry factors like expiring drug patents). Provide separate series for general patent cases, ANDA cases, and appellates for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Active Districts
rubrics_metrics.description: District-level counts and proportions of patent cases filed (e.g., top districts and their percent of total cases over the three-year period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both per-year and multi-year totals and percentages to show concentration (e.g., top three districts may account for >50% of filings). Consider local orders and venue reassignment rules when interpreting year-to-year changes in district activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Active Judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge-level counts of patent cases presided over in a given period (broken down by year and total), with percent of overall patent caseload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use judge-level analytics to inform strategy and timing forecasts; be mindful that assignment patterns or standing orders (e.g., reassignment rules) can shift volumes among judges year-to-year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Active Parties (Plaintiffs / Defendants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of cases filed by the most active plaintiffs and counts of cases in which the most active defendants appeared (including breakdowns by year and districts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify plaintiffs (e.g., monetizers versus operating companies) and defendants (e.g., technology, pharmaceutical) and report multi-year trends; identify which parties dominate filings in particular years and districts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Active Firms and Attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalized counts of law firms and individual attorneys appearing in patent cases (plaintiff-side and defendant-side), including the percentage of those cases that involve HVPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize counsel names from dockets; show districts and HVP percentages to indicate firm/attorney specialization and experience. Use these metrics for opposing-counsel research and hiring/retention decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: Time-to-Event Metrics & Boxplots
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing analytics to key milestones (median and distributional measures). Examples reported: median time to summary judgment = 814 days; median time to trial = 1,091 days; median time to termination = 205 days (for all patent cases terminated 2021–2023, excluding ANDA cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present distributions via box plots (median, interquartile range, whiskers); emphasize variability (e.g., wide range to trial). Use judge-level and claim-level filters to refine forecasting and budgeting. See 'Understanding Box Plots' for interpretation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Resolutions (resolution taxonomy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorization of how cases terminate: likely settlement, procedural resolution (dismissal, contested dismissal, consolidation, stay, transfers, MDL), claimant wins and claim defendant wins by resolution type (default judgment, consent judgment, judgment on the pleadings, summary judgment, trial, JMOL), class action settlements, and open/no resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts and percentages for each resolution type. Note that the majority of district court patent cases in 2021–2023 resolved by likely settlement or procedural grounds (~91% combined); substantive claimant wins outnumber defendant wins when only substantive terminations are considered, but claim defendants prevail more often at summary judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings by Judgment Event
rubrics_metrics.description: Track patent-specific findings at litigation events (judgment on the pleadings, summary judgment/claim construction, trial): Infringement, No Infringement, Invalidity, No Invalidity, Unenforceability, No Unenforceability, and counts by event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count findings at each stage (a case can have findings at multiple stages). Report where findings most frequently occur (e.g., courts found Infringement most often overall—many at default; No Infringement was most common at summary judgment and trial). Use these patterns to assess likelihood of success at different litigation stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Invalidity Reasons (taxonomy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific statutory and doctrinal grounds for invalidity tracked: Subject Matter (101), Anticipation/Novelty (102), Obviousness (103), Definiteness (112), Enablement (112), Written Description (112), Improper Design Patent (171), Defective Correction / Obviousness-Type Double Patenting / other codes, and 'No Invalidity Reason Specified.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts by judgment event and note common loci (e.g., 101/subject-matter invalidity is frequently found at judgment on the pleadings; indefiniteness often appears at claim construction). Provide these breakdowns to inform motion practice and claim-drafting strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages: Types and Yearly Totals
rubrics_metrics.description: Track total patent damages awarded by year (excluding fees, costs, interest) and whether awards were later reversed on appeal; damage types annotated include Enhanced Damages, Lost Profits, Reasonable Royalty, Attorneys' Fees/Costs, Other/Mixed, and Prejudgment Interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts and dollar totals per year and per damage type. Note reversal lag (recent large awards may later be reversed), and highlight notable aggregates (e.g., $6 billion in Reasonable Royalty awards across 129 cases from 2021–2023). Distinguish awards that have been reversed vs. those left standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Petitions and Filing Trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual counts of PTAB petitions (2014–2023) disaggregated by petition type (IPR, PGR, CBM), showing multi-year trends and the end of CBM reviews after 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret filing changes in light of doctrinal and procedural shifts (e.g., Federal Circuit / USPTO standard changes in 2019, Fintiv discretionary denials). Present petition-type breakdowns since case composition (IPR vs. PGR) matters for strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Trial Flow and Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow from Petition → Institution Decision → Final Decision with percentages: out of petitioned trials, report percent denied institution, percent instituted, and final outcomes (All Claims Unpatentable, Mixed Findings, All Claims Upheld, All Claims Amended, Petitioner Win, Patent Owner Win, Procedural Dismissal, Settled, Patent Owner Disclaimed, Joined To Other Trial, etc.). Example percentages reported for 2021–2023: Instituted 54%, Denied Institution 21%, All Claims Unpatentable 22%, All Claims Upheld 6%, Mixed Claim Findings 6%, Procedurally Dismissed 10%, Settled 15%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the whole pipeline to convey attrition and success rates. Note policy shifts (e.g., reduction in discretionary Fintiv denials correlated with increasing institution rates) and provide both petition- and institution-stage statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Appeals Reversal Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Reversal rate for PTAB appeals decided on the merits (reporting 22% reversal for federal PTAB appellate cases terminated 2021–2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute reversal rate as Reversed + Affirmed/Reversed_in_Part divided by total Reversed/Affirmed/Reversed_in_Part cases; report alongside affirmance rate to capture appellate dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-Originating Federal Appellate Cases (metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of federal appellate dockets originating from patent cases over time and timing to termination (median near one year after docketing for terminated appellate cases). Report reversal rate for district-court appeals (34% reversal for patent cases terminated 2021–2023 with decision on merits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide per-year docket counts and time-to-termination distributions. Use reversal-rate methodology consistent with PTAB calculations; explain calculation in footnote for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Methodology Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Data sourced from Lex Machina’s platform using machine learning and technology-assisted attorney review; raw sources include PACER. Raw data is cleaned, normalized (judges, parties, firms, attorneys), tagged, structured, and annotated (case resolutions, damages, dispositive rulings). The platform updates daily; report snapshots reflect publication date (February 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose extraction/normalization steps, limitations, and update cadence. Note that corrections and future PACER updates may change counts; provide users means to replicate filters and reproduce figures on the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding Box Plots (visualization guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box plots summarize distributions using five numbers: median, upper and lower quartiles, and whiskers for the distribution. The box encloses the middle 50% (25th to 75th percentile); the median line splits the data in half; whiskers show outside bounds of reasonable expectation (outliers defined by >1.5× IQR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use box plots to convey medians and variability; interpret compressed vs. elongated boxes (compressed = more consistent, elongated = less predictable). Include explanation in reports so readers correctly interpret timing analytics.
